# How to read this book {.unnumbered}

**If you are new to machine learning,** read the book in order. Chapters 1 to 4 are the foundation: what a probability means, how to check it, and how to turn it into an action. Chapters 5 and 6 give a short, simple tour of neural networks, LLMs and AI agents.

**If you already work with LLMs,** still read Chapters 3 and 4, because everything after them depends on these two chapters. Then continue from Chapter 7.

**If you lead a team or a product,** read Chapters 1 to 4, then Chapters 7, 10, 11, 13 and 15. After that, you will be able to ask your team the four questions that matter most: What does a mistake cost? Where is the threshold? Can we trust the probabilities? Who checks the warnings?

## The boxes

A **Key idea** box, with a thick bar on its left, holds one lesson worth remembering: a bold headline you can repeat to a colleague, and one sentence that explains why it is true. At the end of each chapter, a **Keep these** box lists all the key ideas of that chapter.

A **Where this breaks** box shows the limits of what the chapter just explained. Please read these boxes carefully; they tell you when a method can be trusted and when it cannot.

A **Set the threshold** box gives you a small decision to make, with real costs. The answer is given in brackets.

A **Going deeper** box has optional maths. You can skip it; nothing later depends on it.

Each chapter ends with one exercise. Try it before you turn the page; the answers are at the back of the book.
